plants.name: Tulsi (Holy Basil)
plants.description: Revered in AYUSH tradition as the 'Queen of Herbs' and an adaptogen that promotes longevity, mental balance, and respiratory wellness.
plants.appearance: Upright aromatic subshrub with green to purple serrated leaves, square stems, and spires of purple-white flowers.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Warm, sunny courtyards, well-lit balconies, and east-facing windowsills
plants.soil: Rich, well-draining loamy soil with organic compost (pH 6.0 - 7.5)
plants.sunlight: High (5-6 hours direct morning sun)
plants.watering: Moderate (allow top inch of soil to dry between waterings)
plants.vastuExplanation: Traditionally revered in Vastu Shastra as the most auspicious plant for North, East, and North-East (Ishanya corner), considered to harmonize spiritual energy and bring serenity.
plants.traditionalUses: Traditionally used for respiratory ease, relieving mild cough, promoting digestion, and as an adaptogen for natural resilience.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh leaves brewed into warm infusion with ginger, or taken as leaf decoction (Kwath/Kashayam).
plants.precautions: Educational context: May moderately affect blood clotting when taken in high concentrated doses. Not a substitute for medical emergency treatment.

plants.name: Ashwagandha (Indian Ginseng)
plants.description: A premier Rasayana (rejuvenator) in Ayurveda renowned for nourishing vital energy (Ojas), combating fatigue, and promoting restful sleep.
plants.appearance: Small woody shrub with dull green elliptic leaves, tiny bell-shaped yellow-green flowers, and bright red berries in papery calyces.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Warm semi-arid climate, dry sunny garden beds, and medium planters
plants.soil: Sandy loam or light dry soil with excellent drainage (pH 7.5 - 8.0)
plants.sunlight: High (Full sun, drought tolerant)
plants.watering: Low (Very drought tolerant, sensitive to root rot)
plants.vastuExplanation: Traditionally associated with vitality, strength, and grounding energy when placed along East or South-East zones.
plants.traditionalUses: Traditionally valued for stamina, stress balance, nervous system rejuvenation, and supporting restorative sleep.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fine root powder (Churna) traditionally mixed with warm milk and organic honey at bedtime.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Avoid during active pregnancy without practitioner supervision. Consult healthcare provider if having thyroid or autoimmune conditions.

plants.name: Aloe Vera (Ghritkumari)
plants.description: Known in traditional texts as Ghritkumari, this cooling succulent is celebrated for skin rejuvenation, liver support, and soothing digestion.
plants.appearance: Stemless succulent rosette with thick, fleshy lanceolate serrated leaves with translucent gel core.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Sunny indoor windowsills, balconies, dry warm verandas
plants.soil: Cactus or succulent potting mix, well-draining sandy soil
plants.sunlight: Medium to High (Bright indirect to gentle direct sunlight)
plants.watering: Low (Water thoroughly only when soil is completely dry)
plants.vastuExplanation: In traditional Vastu, Aloe Vera is considered to attract positive ambient energy and purify living spaces when kept in the East or North.
plants.traditionalUses: Topical soothing for skin irritations, traditional digestive tonic, cooling Pitta dosha.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh inner leaf gel rinsed thoroughly to remove yellow aloin latex before topical or culinary use.
plants.precautions: Educational context: The yellow latex beneath the rind has potent laxative properties; use inner transparent gel only.

plants.name: Neem (Indian Lilac)
plants.description: Known as 'Arishta' (reliever of sickness) in Sanskrit, Neem is the cornerstone of AYUSH blood purification and skin health.
plants.appearance: Graceful tree with pinnate compound bright green serrated leaflets and fragrant small white star blossoms.
plants.height: Pruned container: 1 - 2 m (Can grow larger in ground)
plants.growthHabit: Fast-growing evergreen tree (can be kept in large pots)
plants.suitableEnvironment: Outdoor courtyards, terraces, backyards with plenty of warmth
plants.soil: Tolerates poor soils; prefers deep sandy-clay loam
plants.sunlight: High (Full blazing sun)
plants.watering: Low to Moderate (Deep watering once weekly)
plants.spaceRequired: Large (3 x 3 ft in deep containers)
plants.vastuExplanation: Traditionally positioned in outer compound or North-West/West to filter incoming breezes and ward off pests and negative energy.
plants.traditionalUses: Skin clarifying, oral hygiene (Datun), natural antimicrobial support, traditional blood purifier.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh leaf water bath for skin soothing; paste of leaves applied externally.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Highly bitter; internal use of seed oil is contraindicated. Excessive internal consumption not advised.

plants.name: Brahmi (Water Hyssop)
plants.description: Renowned 'Medhya Rasayana' (intellect promoter) in Ayurveda and Siddha, celebrated for enhancing memory, focus, and cognitive tranquility.
plants.appearance: Creeping succulent herb with small oblong fleshy leaves and delicate white-blue 4-5 lobed flowers.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Moist planters, indoor water trays, shaded balconies, near water features
plants.soil: Rich wet, boggy or aquatic potting soil, high organic matter
plants.sunlight: Medium (Partial shade to filtered morning sun)
plants.watering: High (Soil must remain constantly damp; thrives with moist tray)
plants.spaceRequired: Small (1 x 1 ft or hanging basket)
plants.vastuExplanation: Associated with wisdom, Saraswati energy, and mental peace; ideally positioned in quiet North or North-East study areas.
plants.traditionalUses: Sharpening memory, easing mental fatigue, nervous relaxation, traditional hair oils.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Ghee cooked with Brahmi juice (Brahmi Ghrita) or fresh leaf tea with a drop of honey.
plants.precautions: Educational context: May cause mild digestive upset if taken on an empty stomach. Always consult a certified AYUSH physician.

plants.name: Giloy / Guduchi (Heart-leaved Moonseed)
plants.description: Celebrated as 'Amrita' (nectar of immortality) in Ayurveda for building deep immune resistance, detoxifying, and balancing all three Doshas.
plants.appearance: Extensive deciduous climbing vine with succulent grooved stems and heart-shaped glossy leaves.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Sunny balcony railings, outdoor garden trellises, compound walls
plants.soil: Well-draining loam to sandy soil
plants.sunlight: Medium to High (Partial sun to full sun)
plants.vastuExplanation: Auspicious climber considered in traditional Indian home planning to weave a protective, vitality-enhancing shield around courtyards.
plants.traditionalUses: Immune defense, regulating recurring mild fevers, digestive fire (Agni) support, liver balance.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh crushed stem boiled into decoction (Kashayam) or concentrated water extract (Guduchi Satva).
plants.precautions: Educational context: Those on blood-sugar medication should monitor levels as Giloy traditionally supports glucose balance.

plants.name: Amla (Indian Gooseberry)
plants.description: One of the richest natural sources of Vitamin C and the cornerstone fruit of Chyawanprash, embodying all tastes except salty.
plants.appearance: Small to medium tree with delicate feathery light-green foliage and pale greenish-yellow globose fruits.
plants.growthHabit: Deciduous small tree or pruned large container shrub
plants.suitableEnvironment: Spacious sunny terraces, garden corners, open courtyards
plants.soil: Deep, well-drained loamy or clay soil with good drainage
plants.sunlight: High (Full direct sun)
plants.vastuExplanation: Traditionally considered sacred and spiritually pure; Vastu assigns it to East or North-East to foster family prosperity and health.
plants.traditionalUses: Anti-aging Rasayana, hair health, digestion, eyesight support, antioxidant resilience.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh fruit juice with honey, dried fruit powder (Triphala component), amla murabba.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Sour and cold potency; consume moderately during late evenings if prone to throat phlegm.

plants.name: Shatavari (Wild Asparagus)
plants.description: Translated as 'She who possesses a hundred husbands', Shatavari is the ultimate feminine tonic, adaptogen, and cooling rejuvenator.
plants.appearance: Climbing thorny subshrub with delicate needle-like cladodes (leaves) and fragrant white tiny blossoms.
plants.growthHabit: Thorny twining woody creeper with tuberous roots
plants.suitableEnvironment: Warm sunny or partial-sun garden spaces, outdoor planters with trellis
plants.soil: Rich well-drained sandy loam soil
plants.sunlight: Medium to High (Partial shade to morning sun)
plants.vastuExplanation: Traditionally associated with nurturing, lunar energy, and feminine harmony in the North and North-West sectors.
plants.traditionalUses: Female reproductive wellness, lactation support, soothing gastric acidity, nourishing Ojas.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Root powder boiled in organic milk with cardamom and raw sugar (Shatavari Ksheerapaka).
plants.precautions: Educational context: Caution advised if sensitive to asparagus family plants or estrogen-sensitive conditions.

plants.name: Lemongrass (Karpuravalli / Cymbopogon)
plants.description: A fast-growing fragrant grass widely utilized in Unani and Ayurveda for digestive invigoration, soothing headaches, and refreshing beverages.
plants.appearance: Dense tussock grass with long slender arching aromatic leaves smelling intensely of fresh lemon.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Sunny balconies, terrace gardens, outdoor border edges
plants.soil: Rich, sandy well-draining soil
plants.sunlight: High (Full sun, at least 6 hours)
plants.vastuExplanation: Citrus aroma is believed in traditional spatial practices to dispel stale air, promote mental alertness, and uplift ambient mood.
plants.traditionalUses: Digestive gas relief, soothing nervous tension, herbal teas for cold and mild congestion.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Stalks bruised and simmered into herbal tea with mint, cinnamon, and honey.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Highly safe culinary herb; essential oil must be diluted before topical skin contact.

plants.name: Pudina (Spearmint / Peppermint)
plants.description: A staple in Unani (Tibbi) medicine and Ayurveda (Pudina) for cooling digestive heat, relieving nausea, and refreshing the senses.
plants.appearance: Fast-spreading herbaceous ground cover with crinkled bright green serrated leaves and square aromatic stems.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Kitchen windowsills, shady balconies, standalone pots to contain roots
plants.soil: Rich moist potting compost, pH 6.5 - 7.0
plants.sunlight: Medium (Morning sun with afternoon shade)
plants.watering: Moderate to High (Likes damp, fertile soil)
plants.vastuExplanation: Associated with freshness, clarity of conversation, and cooling excess fire in northern and eastern family areas.
plants.traditionalUses: Gas and flatulence relief, cooling summer heat, soothing mild headaches, digestive refresh.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh leaves crushed into cooling mint chutney with cumin or steeped in soothing tea.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Avoid excessive intake if suffering from severe acid reflux (GERD) as mint relaxes the esophageal sphincter.

plants.name: Shankhpushpi (Morning Glory Herb)
plants.description: Famous classical brain tonic used to induce mental peace, relieve anxiety, and support academic focus and memory retention.
plants.appearance: Prostrate spreading herb with small hairy leaves and beautiful solitary conch-shaped light blue or white blossoms.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Warm sunny courtyards, sunny hanging planters, terrace borders
plants.soil: Sandy loam or dry well-drained soil
plants.sunlight: High (Full sun)
plants.vastuExplanation: Traditional Vastu holds blue and white flowering brain tonics in high regard in North-East study areas for academic focus.
plants.traditionalUses: Calming nervous restlessness, promoting sleep quality, cognitive enhancement, mental clarity.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh plant juice or dry powder taken with warm cow's milk and honey in the morning.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Mild hypotensive effect; individuals with very low blood pressure should consult their doctor.

plants.name: Vasaka / Adhatoda (Malabar Nut)
plants.description: Celebrated in Siddha and Ayurveda as the premier bronchodilator herb, rich in the alkaloid vasicine for respiratory comfort.
plants.appearance: Dense evergreen shrub with large lanceolate dark green leaves and white tubular flowers striped with purple veins.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Warm garden beds, sunny patio pots, terrace boundaries
plants.soil: Adaptable to various soils; prefers moist loamy soil
plants.sunlight: Medium to High (Partial shade to full sun)
plants.vastuExplanation: Fosters cleansing vitality and life breath (Prana); recommended near outdoor garden boundaries.
plants.traditionalUses: Easing bronchial spasms, clearing phlegm, supporting healthy lung function in coughs.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh leaf decoction with ginger and black pepper, traditionally prepared as Vasavaleha.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Potent uterine stimulant; strictly contraindicated during pregnancy.

plants.name: Bhringraj (False Daisy)
plants.description: The 'King of Hair' in Siddha and Ayurveda, renowned for restoring natural hair luster, pacifying Pitta, and revitalizing the liver.
plants.appearance: Small erect or creeping herb with dark lanceolate leaves and solitary dainty white daisy-like flower heads.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Moist garden plots, shallow planters, shaded balconies
plants.soil: Rich, moisture-retentive loamy soil
plants.sunlight: Medium (Partial sun to bright dappled shade)
plants.vastuExplanation: Brings tranquil rejuvenating energies, traditionally planted near morning water outlets or north herb patches.
plants.traditionalUses: Deep hair conditioning, preventing premature graying, supporting liver health and vision.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh juice infused into pure coconut or sesame oil (Bhringraj Taila) for scalp massage.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Safe topical herb; cold potency when taken internally in excess during winter.

plants.name: Kalmegh (Green Chiretta / King of Bitters)
plants.description: Famous in AYUSH for its intense bitterness and potent immune-protective, liver-protective, and digestive-stimulating prowess.
plants.appearance: Slender erect annual herb with dark green lanceolate leaves and small white flowers spotted with rose-purple markings.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Warm sunny gardens, terrace pots, monsoon-favored locations
plants.soil: Fertile, moist sandy loam soil with good drainage
plants.sunlight: Medium to High (Morning sun with slight afternoon shade)
plants.vastuExplanation: Symbolizes sharp discernment and purification; dispels sluggishness when positioned along sunny eastern perimeters.
plants.traditionalUses: Natural liver protection, managing seasonal colds and viral fevers, stimulating sluggish appetite.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Decoction of dried leaves (Kashaya) or powdered herb taken with warm water.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Extreme bitter taste; contraindicated in pregnancy due to traditional emmenagogue properties.

plants.name: Turmeric (Haldi / Haridra)
plants.description: The golden jewel of AYUSH medicine, sacred in rituals and unmatched in traditional anti-inflammatory, detoxifying, and skin-beautifying actions.
plants.appearance: Stemless perennial with large broad glossy green leaves rising from fragrant golden-orange rhizomes.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Warm humid balconies, partially shaded verandas, wide growing containers
plants.soil: Loose friable rich composted soil with excellent drainage
plants.sunlight: Medium (Filtered bright light or partial morning sun)
plants.watering: Moderate to High (Keep consistently damp without standing water)
plants.vastuExplanation: Revered as a divine purifier associated with Jupiter (Guru), wealth, and sanctity. Highly auspicious in the North-East zone.
plants.traditionalUses: Natural joint comfort, skin glow (Ubtan), wound cleansing, metabolic balance, golden milk.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh rhizome grated into warm milk with black pepper and ghee (Haldi Doodh).
plants.precautions: Educational context: Therapeutic high-dose extracts may interact with blood thinners. Use culinary quantities freely.

plants.name: Ginger (Adrak / Shunthi)
plants.description: Celebrated as 'Vishwabheshaja' (the universal medicine) for enkindling digestive fire (Agni), relieving nausea, and soothing throat irritation.
plants.appearance: Upright reed-like leafy stems with narrow lanceolate foliage rising from pungent underground knobby rhizomes.
plants.growthHabit: Perennial reed-like herb with underground rhizomes
plants.suitableEnvironment: Warm sheltered balconies, bright verandas, kitchen garden planters
plants.soil: Loose rich organic potting mix with plenty of vermicompost
plants.sunlight: Medium (Dappled sunlight or gentle morning light)
plants.indoorOutdoor: Both (bright indoor spots or covered patio)
plants.vastuExplanation: Represents the Agni (fire) element in harmony; placement in South-East or East activates culinary vitality and warmth.
plants.traditionalUses: Digestive spark, relieving travel nausea, soothing cold and sore throat, comforting winter warmth.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh root sliced and boiled with tea leaves, crushed ginger with rock salt before meals.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Pungent and heating; reduce intake during acute stomach ulcers or burning sensations.

plants.name: Curry Leaf (Kadi Patta / Karivepila)
plants.description: Essential culinary and medicinal treasure in Siddha and Ayurveda, celebrated for antioxidant qualities, digestive tone, and lustrous dark hair.
plants.appearance: Small handsome tropical tree with dark green aromatic pinnate leaves and small white fragrant blossoms.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Warm sunny balconies, backyard garden beds, kitchen-side planters
plants.soil: Fertile slightly acidic to neutral loamy soil with compost
plants.sunlight: High (Full sun, minimum 5 hours)
plants.watering: Moderate (Allow surface soil to dry slightly)
plants.vastuExplanation: Traditionally positioned near kitchen entryways or western verandas to promote nutritional wellness and prosperity.
plants.traditionalUses: Digestive enzyme stimulation, controlling premature gray hair, traditional metabolic support.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh leaves tempered in ghee, or crushed into morning buttermilk with cumin.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Highly safe culinary herb; ensure organic growing without chemical pesticides.

plants.name: Hibiscus / Jaswand (Japa Pushpa)
plants.description: Sacred crimson blossom prized in traditional cosmetics and therapies for strengthening hair roots, cooling blood heat, and calming the mind.
plants.appearance: Vibrant evergreen shrub with glossy oval leaves and dramatic trumpet-shaped five-petaled blossoms with prominent stamens.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Sunny terraces, garden borders, warm balconies
plants.soil: Well-drained rich potting soil high in organic matter
plants.sunlight: High (Full direct sun for abundant blooming)
plants.watering: Moderate to High (Water thoroughly during blooming season)
plants.vastuExplanation: Red hibiscus is sacred to the Sun (Surya) and divine energy; traditionally planted in the East to invoke radiance, energy, and auspiciousness.
plants.traditionalUses: Hair nourishing packs, natural conditioner, cooling herbal teas, menstrual regularity support.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Fresh petals infused into warm hair oil or dried into cooling herbal tea.
plants.precautions: Educational context: May have mild emmenagogue properties; use in standard culinary amounts during pregnancy.

plants.name: Arnica (Mountain Daisy)
plants.description: The primary trauma and bruise remedy in Homeopathy, historically utilized in traditional alpine folk practices for muscular aches.
plants.appearance: Perennial herb with basal rosette of ovate leaves and bright golden-yellow daisy blossoms.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Cooler climate containers, temperate verandas, shaded rockeries
plants.soil: Acidic, nutrient-poor, sandy or peaty well-drained soil
plants.sunlight: Medium to High (Gentle sun, prefers cool roots)
plants.vastuExplanation: Golden blossoms resonate with healing, recovery, and restorative calm when positioned along northern quiet zones.
plants.traditionalUses: Homeopathic preparation for trauma, sprains, post-workout soreness, and localized bruising.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Homeopathically potentized tinctures, topical herbal creams and liniments (external only).
plants.precautions: Educational context: Do not apply arnica herbal extract to broken open skin. Ingest only in potentized homeopathic form under guidance.

plants.name: Calendula (Pot Marigold)
plants.description: Cherished in Homeopathic and Naturopathic traditions as a supreme topical vulnerary for rapid wound soothing and gentle tissue recovery.
plants.appearance: Cheerful bushy annual with aromatic oblong leaves and warm golden-orange daisy flowers that close at dusk.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Sunny balconies, window boxes, garden flower beds
plants.soil: Average well-draining garden soil
plants.sunlight: High (Full sun to light partial shade)
plants.watering: Moderate (Water when top inch is dry)
plants.vastuExplanation: Golden yellow and orange blossoms bring radiant solar warmth, optimism, and positive prana to morning sunlight sectors.
plants.traditionalUses: Gentle skin soothing, minor cuts, sunburn relief, comforting floral teas.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Petals infused in olive or almond oil, or prepared into homeopathic mother tincture.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Individuals with Asteraceae / ragweed family allergies should test topical patch first.

plants.name: Cinnamon / Dalchini (True Cinnamon)
plants.description: Prized across Unani and Ayurvedic traditions for stimulating peripheral circulation, sweetening digestive fires, and aromatic warmth.
plants.appearance: Glossy evergreen tree with ovate thick leaves that flush coppery-red when young, with strongly aromatic inner bark.
plants.growthHabit: Evergreen small tree / large container plant
plants.suitableEnvironment: Warm humid balconies, sunny sheltered verandas
plants.soil: Rich well-drained sandy loam soil with organic matter
plants.sunlight: Medium to High (Warm partial shade to sun)
plants.spaceRequired: Medium to Large (2 x 2 ft pot)
plants.vastuExplanation: Pungent warming spice tree associated with the fire (Agni) element; ideal in the South-East corner to stimulate enterprise and prosperity.
plants.traditionalUses: Metabolic and glucose support, warming cold constitutions, aromatic breath freshness, culinary spice.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Bark boiled with black tea or steeped with hot water and raw honey.
plants.precautions: Educational context: True Ceylon cinnamon contains very low coumarin compared to Cassia; avoid excessive medicinal quantities in pregnancy.

plants.name: Guggulu (Indian Bdellium Tree)
plants.description: Revered in AYUSH tradition for producing fragrant healing oleo-gum resin that scrapes toxins (Ama), supports joint mobility, and maintains lipids.
plants.appearance: Small thorny arid tree with papery peeling bark, sparse leaves, and small reddish flowers.
plants.suitableEnvironment: Dry sunny terraces, arid balconies, sunny rock gardens
plants.soil: Gravelly sandy dry soil with rapid drainage
plants.sunlight: High (Full direct desert sun)
plants.vastuExplanation: Traditional Vastu associates hearty arid protective trees with the grounding South and South-West boundaries for stability.
plants.traditionalUses: Joint comfort, healthy lipid balance, natural metabolic cleansing, fragrant incense.
plants.traditionalPreparation: Traditionally purified in herbal decoctions (Triphala Kwath) before being formulated into tablets.
plants.precautions: Educational context: Purified resin only; contraindicated in acute liver or kidney failure without physician guidance.

quizQuestions.question: Which sacred herb is traditionally referred to as 'Queen of Herbs' and considered most auspicious in the North-East (Ishanya) direction?
quizQuestions.explanation: Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum) is deeply revered in Ayurveda and traditional Vastu Shastra for bringing positive pranic energy, tranquility, and air purification to the North and North-East.

quizQuestions.question: According to traditional Vastu Shastra guidelines, which direction is traditionally associated with the Water/Clarity element and ideal for mind-enhancing herbs like Brahmi?
quizQuestions.explanation: The North-East (Ishanya corner) represents clarity, wisdom, and spiritual focus, making it the traditional choice for Medhya Rasayana herbs such as Brahmi and Tulsi.

quizQuestions.question: Identify this plant: It has thick fleshy succulent leaves filled with soothing transparent gel, widely used in AYUSH for skin soothing and cooling digestion.
quizQuestions.explanation: Aloe Vera (Ghritkumari) is recognized by its thick, spiny-edged succulent leaves and cooling gel used across Ayurveda and Naturopathy.

quizQuestions.question: True or False: Traditional Vastu plant placements are considered scientific medical treatments that cure physical illnesses.
quizQuestions.explanation: False! Vastu guidelines are traditional and cultural architectural recommendations for aesthetic and spatial harmony. They do not constitute scientific medical treatments.

quizQuestions.question: Which AYUSH plant is known as 'Amrita' (nectar of immortality) and grows as a heart-leaved deciduous climbing vine?
quizQuestions.explanation: Giloy (Tinospora cordifolia) is renowned in Ayurveda for deep immune resilience and is distinguished by its heart-shaped leaves and grooved succulent stems.

quizQuestions.question: In Siddha medicine and Ayurveda, which herb is famously hailed as 'Kesharaja' (King of Hair) for promoting hair vitality?
quizQuestions.explanation: Bhringraj is celebrated in Siddha and Ayurvedic literature as the primary botanical for hair nourishment and cooling liver heat.

quizQuestions.question: Identify this aromatic grass: Releases a sharp citrus fragrance, used in Unani herbal teas for digestion and headache relief.
quizQuestions.explanation: Lemongrass forms tall arching aromatic blades with a signature lemon scent, favored in Unani and Ayurvedic soothing beverages.

quizQuestions.question: True or False: Most AYUSH medicinal herbs like Tulsi and Hibiscus require at least 4 to 6 hours of sunlight daily for healthy growth.
quizQuestions.explanation: True! Herbs like Tulsi, Hibiscus, and Lemongrass thrive best in bright morning sun or full sunlight (4-6 hours) to produce their aromatic essential oils.

quizQuestions.question: Which bright golden blossom is the foremost Homeopathic and Naturopathic remedy for topical skin recovery and minor cuts?
quizQuestions.explanation: Calendula officinalis is renowned in Homeopathy as a gentle vulnerary flower that aids skin soothing and comfort.

quizQuestions.question: Which warming spice plant is associated with the Fire (Agni) quadrant (South-East) in traditional home layout principles?
quizQuestions.explanation: Pungent spices like Ginger and Cinnamon represent the warmth of the Fire (Agni) element, traditionally aligned with the South-East corner.
